_meta.change: split the cogPG.PG112 whole-volume CGPG dump into per-work corpus files
_meta.plan_basis: read at the row, with the volume's two halves settled against the TLG Canon's own split and against the served byzantium.gr text. The Canon divides De cerimoniis into two works by EDITION, not by overlapping scope: tlg3023.011 is Vogt (lib. 1.1-92 in Vogt's chapter numbering) and tlg3023.010 is Reiske (lib. 1.84-2.56 in Reiske's). Vogt's 92 book-1 chapters are Reiske's 83, so the two are complementary halves of one text, not an overlap. Measured confirmation, not inference: the served byzantium.gr text's last row ends with the Gothic-game acclamation glossary (σῶσον δὴ σῶσον Ἑβραῖον ... ἡ τροφὴ τῶν στρατευμάτων Ῥωμαῖον), which is the same glossary that closes PG112 locus 354 immediately before its ΚΕΦΑΛ. ΠΔʹ head, and the served text contains nothing of chapter 84 (neither Ἐκ τῶν τοῦ Μαγίστρου Πέτρου nor κόμης τῶν ἀδμηνσιόνων). So the two texts meet exactly at Reiske's chapter 84, each holding one Canon work.
_meta.shared_row_rule: a served row holding a work boundary is assigned to exactly one work, normally the one whose incipit the row carries; the plan records the decision as the ranges themselves
_meta.reversible: To revert: for every carved work file listed under 'works', drop its rows whose locus starts 'PG112.' (delete the file when it was 'created'), strip the 'PG112.' prefix from their loci, re-insert them and the archived 'dropped_duplicates' rows into data/corpus/cogPG.PG112.jsonl together with the residual rows, sorted by locus, and restore data/cgpg_works.json, data/tlg_crosswalk.json/.tsv, and data/corrections_log/provenance.json from the parent commit (or simply git revert the commit; old sha256 below verifies). Every moved row's text is byte-identical; only urn and locus changed.

works.evidence: Reiske's chapters 84 to the end. The block opens mid-row: locus 354 carries the tail of chapter 83's Gothic ceremony and its acclamation glossary (37 tokens, the last thing the served Vogt text also holds) and then the ΚΕΦΑΛ. ΠΔʹ head at character 249, after which the row is chapter 84 (224 tokens). Under the shared-row rule the row goes to the work whose head it carries, so those 37 tokens travel with .010; the deviation is under-claimed nowhere and over-claimed here, and is recorded rather than smoothed. Book 2 opens at locus 495 (ΚΕΦΑΛΑΙΟΝ Αʹ). 73,431 tokens against the Canon's 76,649 words for this work, 0.958, and the shortfall is located: see partial_ceiling below.

residual.note: 44-353 is Reiske's chapters 1-83, the SAME text byzantium.gr serves as tlg3023.011 (75,862 tokens here against 75,843 served). It is left uncarved on purpose: displacing it to corpus_secondary as an edition witness is the disposition cisco reserved on issue #8, and the precedent (PG067, PG113's De thematibus) points that way because a manual transcription beats our OCR of the same text. Nothing about it is unknown; it is waiting on a decision, not on evidence.

corrections_mirror_note: data/corrections_log/applied.jsonl keys this volume's corrections by bare column locus under cogPG.PG112; per the rekey_corrections_log.py convention for cogPG.* bare-locus rows they are left unchanged (historical). The locus map above makes the linkage reconstructable.
